issues.failure_explanation: Definition def:01(i) defines $U^\varepsilon = \{x \in M : V(x) \le \varepsilon\}$ as a subset of the state manifold $M$, and Definition def:01(iii) defines $U^\varepsilon_{h,\alpha}$ as the union of Euler segments emanating from $U^\varepsilon$. The theorem claims $U^\varepsilon_{h,\beta/h} \subseteq U^\varepsilon$. This inclusion is false as stated: one-step maps of the surrogate system do not preserve $M$ (e.g., an Euler step of the rigid-body system sends $R \in SO(3)$ to $R + hR\hat\Omega - \beta\nabla_R V$, which leaves $SO(3)$ for generic $Ω$, $R ∈ SO(3)$), yet the tube must then contain those off-manifold points, which cannot lie in $U^\varepsilon \subseteq M$. Moreover, even under the natural repair (ambient sublevel sets $\{x \in U : V(x) \le \varepsilon\}$), the proof never establishes the claimed inclusion: its escape/contradiction argument only shows that each segment $S_k$ stays in the fattened set $;V ≤ ε+Δ$ and that endpoints satisfy $V(x_{k+1}) ≤ ε$; intermediate segment points with $V ∈ (ε, ε+Δ]$ are never excluded, so the tube inclusion (and hence the derived conclusion $L(h,\alpha) = L$ used for the 'Moreover' optimality claim) is unsupported as written.

failure_location.quote: there exists $h_0 > 0$ such that for each $0 < h < h_0$, $U^\varepsilon_{h, \frac{\beta}{h}} \subseteq U^\varepsilon$ and thus $V^{-1}([0, \varepsilon])$ is positive invariant under respective discrete systems~\eqref{eq:feedback_discrete_system} defined with $\alpha = \frac{\beta}{h}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the sublevel sets in Definition def:01 ambiently ($U^\varepsilon = \{x \in U : V(x) \le \varepsilon\}$) and restate Theorem thm:optimal_a with ambient sets; then add a short contained argument controlling intermediate segment points (along the segment the descent quadratic in $t$ is convex, so its maximum over $t\in[0,1]$ is attained at the endpoints, which gives $V \le \varepsilon$ on the whole tube for small $h$); otherwise weaken the theorem's first claim to endpoint invariance plus containment of segments in the $Δ$-fattened sublevel set.
issues.overall_effect: The first claim of Theorem thm:optimal_a (tube inclusion, and with it the 'Moreover' optimality clause that rests on $L(h,\alpha)=L$ under that inclusion) is false as stated. The same defective set convention is used in the proofs of Theorems thm:adaptive_a and thm:adaptive_a_period (suprema $F_\varepsilon, M_\varepsilon$ over $U^\varepsilon$ and the Łojasiewicz bound are applied at iterates that leave $M$), so those guarantees are also unreliable as written, although their substance (positive invariance of $V^{-1}([0,\varepsilon])$) survives the ambient-set repair.
issues.title: Theorem thm:optimal_a claims a tube inclusion that is false under its own definition and unproven under the ambient reading
issues.why_classification: The resolution is contained: a definitional repair plus a short (contained, nontrivial) convexity argument for intermediate segment points, or a limited weakening of the inclusion claim; the positive-invariance guarantee and the gain rule $\alpha = 1/(hL)$ survive as a recognizably comparable result, so the issue is moderate rather than minor or serious.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: When the noise term is absent (i.e., $f(x) \equiv 0$) and $\nabla V$ is $L$--Lipschitz on $U^\varepsilon$, choosing $\beta \in \left(0, \frac{2}{L}\right)$ yields the basic convergence characteristics of vanilla gradient descent: $U^\varepsilon$ is positively invariant, and if $V$ additionally satisfies the Polyak--Łojasiewicz inequality, then one obtains a sublinear convergence rate for $V(x_k)$.

The remark asserts that, for $f \equiv 0$ with $ħ∇V$ $L$-Lipschitz and $ eta \in (0, 2/L)$, the Polyak-Łojasiewicz inequality yields a sublinear convergence rate for $V(x_k)$. Under the PL inequality $|
abla V|^2 \ge 2\mu(V - V^*)$ and the descent lemma $V(x -  eta
abla V(x)) \le V(x) -  eta(1 - L eta/2)|
abla V(x)|^2$, the values satisfy $V(x_{k+1}) \le (1 - 2\mu eta(1 - L eta/2))(V(x_k) - V^*)$, i.e., linear (geometric) convergence of $V(x_k)$ to $V^* = 0$ — a strictly stronger, not sublinear, guarantee. The paper thus states a materially weaker (and false-as-written) rate claim than what its own assumptions deliver.

failure_location.quote: and if $V$ additionally satisfies the Polyak--Łojasiewicz inequality, then one obtains a sublinear convergence rate for $V(x_k)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'sublinear convergence rate' by 'linear convergence rate' (geometric contraction of $V(x_k) - V^*$ at factor $1 - 2\mu\beta(1 - L\beta/2)$ per step).
issues.overall_effect: Only the side remark's convergence-rate statement is wrong; no labelled theorem, algorithm, or advertised guarantee of the paper depends on it.
issues.title: Remark overclaims a sublinear rate under the Polyak-Łojasiewicz inequality
issues.why_classification: A one-word local correction that preserves every substantive claim and guarantee of the paper; no new argument is required.
